issues.cell: law 1 (10)'s one plain shape-lock rule "no op makes or deepens (*commit*) a meeting with a shape-held thing:" x its colon list x *commit*'s newly x the check's "(9) and (10) by the meetings the commit made newly or deepened" x Part A's J150 sentence and correction 6 x *Carried way*, veto 12, veto 23, E-P1, E-P9, J149's program reading (adj l. 472-477, 429-431, 620-621, 250, 664-666, 525-529, 743-746, 784-790, 2068-2070, 2111-2113; PROGRESS l. 206, 208, 209)
issues.claim: Pass 7 merged law 1 (10) into one plain rule whose lead bars every meeting an op makes or deepens with a shape-held thing, while its own colon list, veto 23's dash list, *Carried way*'s and veto 12's re-route of a raised road's way through a gate of a shape-locked wall, E-P1 (a shape-locked wall 'never merged into'), E-P9 (only a shape-locked raised way's `vault`-use spans' strips impassable) and J149's program reading ('the aqueduct passes over it') bar only the meetings that change it. On ops that are no undo, redo, re-grade, value edit within a standing meeting or repair - a hand aqueduct over a shape-locked ring clearing its top (law 1 (2)'s over, nothing of the ring changed), a hand wall under a shape-locked aqueduct's `open`-use span or beneath a shape-locked viaduct, a hand raised road whose carried way passes a shape-locked ring's standing gate, a wall merged round a shape-locked aqueduct's pier - builder A (the list, J147 (3)'s 'the shape-locked wall never changes') applies each; builder B (the lead as written, as Part A's 'read as written for every op', correction 6's 'every list ... of lawful crossings, impassables ... reading so' and the check have it) bars each as a meeting made newly: every aqueduct into a shape-locked town refused (a closed ring cannot be bent round), *Carried way*'s shape-locked branch left with no lawful outcome. Two maps on the commonest gestures by canvas and clerk; section 5.3's row and T110-4 (c) follow either. Pass 6's (10) bound what a shape-held thing takes from a meeting; pass 7's merge opened the class.
issues.required_change: Law 1 (10): "and no op makes or deepens (*commit*) a meeting with a shape-held thing:" -> "and no meeting an op makes or deepens (*commit*) changes a shape-held thing:" (-1 word), the colon's list standing as what such a change is; conform Part A's J150 sentence, correction 6, veto 23 and E-S13's T110-4 (c) ("no op makes or deepens a meeting with a shape-locked thing (side)" -> "no meeting an op makes or deepens changes a shape-locked thing (side)"). Alternative if every meeting is meant: keep the lead, strike the colon's list, *Carried way*'s and veto 12's re-route through a gate of a shape-locked wall, E-P1's 'a shape-locked one never merged into', E-P9's '`vault`-use spans'' and J149's reading 'passes over it', and say in the veto list that a shape-locked ring bars every raised way, its carried way included.

issues.cell: law 1 (10)'s first half "a thing held in shape its shape, changed by no op but one that names it" x *shape* (the soft readings, an arch vault's chamber and, for a shape lock, outline and size besides) x *held* ('holds its outline and size') x *The soft readings* x veto 23 x the check (outline and size) x Part P pass 7's re-check of PRB7E-LCK-04 x item 110 (b) (adj l. 472-473, 397-401, 388-389, 512-515, 787-788, 624-626, 3803-3804, 832-834; adj@c3411d0 l. 461-462, 374-375, 478-479, 499, 592)
issues.claim: Pass 7 struck the five clauses that read law 1 (10)'s first half down to a meeting made or deepened after the lock ((10)'s 'takes nothing newly ... nor a deeper reading' with 'its readings then following what stands', *held*'s and *Entry*'s 'no soft reading from a meeting made or deepened after its lock', *The soft readings*' 'none falls newly', (G2)'s), leaving 'a thing held in shape its shape, changed by no op but one that names it' with the *shape* term that includes the soft readings and the chamber. A hand delete (`wallToWay`, `dismantle`) of a wall run under a shape-locked aqueduct's `open`-read `vault`-use span, or a hand delete of a road deck (or breach of its span) over a ring shape-locked while capped, names the other side and changes the shape-held thing's readings (the span read `vault` and its chamber laid; the run's top back up). Builder A (*held*'s 'outline and size', *The soft readings*, veto 23's 'a reading it had follows what stands when the other side goes', pass 7's 'PRB7E-LCK-04 ... applies', the check) applies it; builder B (law 1 (10)'s words with the term they name) refuses it by hand (`refuse.raised.meeting`) and waits it at an epoch - so the user cannot remove a raised way over a shape-locked capped run, against item 110 (b)'s 'the user may add or remove a raised way' as R7-02 keeps it, and the lock holds more than the 'outline and size only' J147 records (the program's reading). PRB7E-LCK-04's closure rests on words no longer in Part L and fails; no lock behaviour under an undo, redo, re-grade or repair is involved.
issues.required_change: Law 1 (10), one sentence closing this finding with PRB7H-LCK-01: "10. a thing held in placement keeps its placement and a thing held in shape its outline and size (*held*), changed by no op but one that names it - a meeting changing a placement-held thing's shape alone (J144) -, and no meeting an op makes or deepens (*commit*) changes a shape-held thing: no wall-like line, band or strip newly across the strip of a `vault`-use span of it, no aqueduct merged into it, no soffit lowered over a run of it, no gate made in it, its readings else following what stands (J147; J150, its behaviour under the ops Part A names round 8's; J146, PRB7E-LCK-04; PRB7F-LCK-01, PRB7F-GEN-01);" - cutting the parenthesis' restatement of Part A pays for the additions: the clause goes from 119 to 108 words, which also pays for PRB7H-LCK-03's and -04's additions (+6, +3), so Part L does not grow.

issues.cell: the Terms' lead "law 1 reads each one's own strip ... a thing lawful only where it is so against each, and a move or search keeping a thing clear of them reads their union" x law 1 (5), (6)'s aqueduct over-crossing exception x law 2 (a)'s 'the lawful shape law 3 picks nearest it' x correction 7 x R7-02 *Strips, zones and nearest points*' *Several raised ways* x W13 x E-S4's union variant (adj l. 314-316, 456-460, 539-549, 675-676, 1004-1006, 1299, 1817-1820, 618-620)
issues.claim: Pass 7 (PRB7G-LCK-04, -GEN-05) gave law 1 a per-raised-way reading and the moves that keep a thing clear the union. Where a declared viaduct D and an aqueduct A stand side by side over a ring laid after D and crossed by A over (A's spans clearing the ring and a tower's or gatehouse's top), a hand stroke's S7 tower falling in D's strip near A, a gate placed (`placeGate`, canvas or clerk) or slid by its grip into D's strip, or a hand stroke's anchor or river crossing in D's zone, must leave D's strip or zone: builder A (law 2 (a) and law 3's nearest lawful shape, correction 7's 'standing under the aqueduct only in an over crossing whose spans clear it') stops it just past D's edge under A's clearing arch; builder B (the Terms' union for moves, *Several raised ways*' 'moved out of all, never into another', W13's nearer edge of the union, E-S4's 'none moved from one into the other') carries it past A's strip too, tens of metres along an oblique ring or back to D's far side. Two towers, gates or anchors for one gesture; section 5.3's row passes both and E-S4's fixture fails builder A. A class pass 7's own refinement opened.
issues.required_change: Terms' lead: "and a move or search keeping a thing clear of them reads their union" -> "and a move or search keeping a thing clear of them reads their union, stopping where law 1 admits it" (+6 words, paid by PRB7H-LCK-02's cut). Examples conformed: *Several raised ways* "so a thing kept or moved out of one is kept or moved out of all, never into another" -> "so a thing kept or moved out of one stops only where section 2.7's laws admit it against all"; E-S4's "every tower, gate and fixed place clear of the union of their strips and zones, none moved from one into the other" -> "every tower, gate and fixed place where section 2.7's laws admit it against both raised ways (law 1 (5), (6)), none moved into a strip or zone that bars it". Alternative if the union is meant: law 1 (5)'s exception adds "where the thing was not moved there out of another raised way's strip or zone", correction 7 and veto 6 naming it.

issues.cell: *Carried way*'s "its gate at the first point beyond the foot: by hand section 7.3's S7 operator makes it in every wall the declared way crosses" and "Where the wall is shape-locked, or its gate law gives the way no lawful gate there, ... re-routed by law 2 (b) from the first point beyond the foot through the nearest gate" x *beyond the foot* (one point, the nearest past the foot) x law 2's order and (a)'s 'a crossing along the line it crosses' x E-D1 x PRB7D-LCK-10's closure (adj l. 516-529, 352-355, 486-488, 540-541, 2161-2162, 3043; adj@c3411d0 l. 500-502)
issues.claim: Pass 7 put a place into *Carried way*'s lead (written for PRB7G-GEN-01's stage-1 gate) that now governs the hand path: the gate 'at the first point beyond the foot', a single point of the carried way a few metres past the foot set by the deck and the wall's width. (1) A hand raised road (canvas or the clerk's `drawWay { raised: true }`) whose deck lands 40 m short of a walled town, its declared way running on through an outer and an inner ring: builder A (pass 6's words, E-D1's 'every held wall it crosses ... to the stroke's end') makes a gate where the way crosses each ring; builder B finds no wall at the first point beyond the foot, so 'its gate law gives the way no lawful gate there', and re-routes the way by law 2 (b) through each ring's nearest existing gate, else refuses the stroke - and two walls can never both have their gate at that one point. (2) Where the way meets the ring's line on a standing tower's footprint, law 2 (a) would slide the op's own crossing along the ring past the tower ('a crossing along the line it crosses'; PRB7D-LCK-10's 'the stroke bent'), but the pinned place lets (a) only shift the deck sideways, else (b) sends the way to the nearest existing gate: three builds. Two outcomes or none on the commonest hand gesture into a walled town; section 5.3's gate row passes each; PRB7D-LCK-10's closure fails in part.
issues.required_change: *Carried way*: "its gate at the first point beyond the foot: by hand" -> "its gate where its ground course crosses that wall beyond the foot: by hand" (+2 words); "or its gate law gives the way no lawful gate there" -> "or law 2 (a) leaves the way no lawful gate in it" (+1), so the op's own crossing moves along the wall first (law 2 (a), law 3) and the re-route 'from the first point beyond the foot through the nearest gate' stays law 2 (b)'s. Alternative if the fixed place is meant: "by hand the deck brought down so that the declared way crosses each wall there, else ...", named in the veto list as a re-shape of the user's stroke.

issues.cell: Part P pass 7's PRB7G-GEN-04 row "a gate or way laid later under an arch passes by the rule" (adj l. 3771) x law 2 (a)'s "for a way, a gate's too, laid beneath a standing raised way" x correction 7's and veto 6's "a gate's way laid after it" x base section 4.3's "laid after it" x W2's last cell and the bent group's (iv) (adj l. 535-537, 675-676, 711-712, 1288, 1186-1187; base l. 5743-5747)
issues.claim: A hand drawWall (W2) passing beneath an aqueduct over (its span clearing the wall and a gatehouse) makes a gate for an older street - laid before the aqueduct, which crossed it at 50 degrees to its deck - inside the aqueduct's strip. The laws (law 2 (a) read with correction 7, veto 6 and section 4.3's 'laid after it') bind the crossing rule only to a gate's way laid after the aqueduct, so the gate stands under the clearing arch (law 1 (5)) and the stroke is not bent; the PRB7G-GEN-04 row's 'a gate ... laid later under an arch passes by the rule' binds it to the gate, so the oblique street fails, the gate moves along it out of the strip and the stroke is bent through it (W2's last cell, as written). An example against the laws.
issues.required_change: The PRB7G-GEN-04 row: "a gate or way laid later under an arch passes by the rule" -> "a way laid later under an arch, a gate's among them, passes by the rule; a gate a later wall makes on an older way takes that way as it stands". Optionally law 2 (a)'s "for a way, a gate's too, laid beneath" -> "for a way, a gate's way too, laid beneath" (+1 word) so the participle cannot attach to the gate.
